_comment: System and Information Integrity Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs with AU (SI-4 system monitoring feeds the audit pipeline), IR (SI-3 malware + SI-7 integrity findings generate incident signals), and RA (SI-2 flaw remediation consumes RA-5 vulnerability scans). Broadest of the Tier 1 plans — 23 base controls in the catalog.
title: System and Information Integrity Plan
description: Documents how the system identifies, reports, and remediates flaws; protects against malicious code; monitors system events; and maintains the integrity of software, firmware, and information. Covers the controls of the SI family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-40 r4 (Patch Management), NIST SP 800-83 r1 (Malware), NIST SP 800-94 (IDS/IPS), and NIST SP 800-115 (Technical Guide to Information Security Testing).
intro_template:
This System and Information Integrity Plan documents the integrity-protection approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, tooling, cadences, and roles used to detect and remediate flaws, prevent malicious code execution, monitor system behavior, validate inputs, and maintain the integrity of software, firmware, and stored information.

The scope covers vulnerability management and patching, malicious-code protection, system monitoring, security alerts and advisories, integrity verification of software / firmware / information, input validation, error handling, and information lifecycle within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (System and Information Integrity family), NIST SP 800-40 r4 (Patch Management), and NIST SP 800-83 r1 (Malware Incident Prevention and Handling).
approach_template:
{system_name} relies on {vuln_scan_tool} for vulnerability scanning, {malware_tool} for malicious-code protection, and {monitoring_tool} for system monitoring. Patches are deployed per the SLA tiers in §4.2. Security alerts and advisories are ingested from {alert_sources}. Integrity of software, firmware, and configuration baselines is verified through {integrity_mechanism}.

Additional details on flaw remediation, malicious-code protection, system monitoring, alert ingestion, integrity verification, input validation, error handling, and information management are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Integrity-related performance for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (patch SLA compliance per severity tier, MTTR for critical vulnerabilities, malware detection-and-removal time, alert false-positive rate, integrity-verification coverage). Vulnerability scans run on the cadence in §6.2, with results feeding the patching queue and the POA&M. The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog is monitored continuously and any KEV entry affecting the system triggers expedited handling.
integration_template: This System and Information Integrity Plan does not stand alone. The AU family records integrity-related events for analysis; the IR family handles incidents detected through SI-3 / SI-4 / SI-7 signals; the RA family supplies vulnerability data via RA-5 scanning; the CM family deploys patches and integrity-protected baselines via the change-control workflow. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where SI-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Enterprise vulnerability-management program (when shared scanning + patch infrastructure)
Enterprise security-alert subscription service (CISA / vendor advisories)
Enterprise email security gateway (spam / phishing protection)

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: Tooling and one-line summaries that anchor the rest of the plan.

questions.label: Vulnerability scanning tool
questions.help: Primary scanner (e.g., 'Tenable.sc', 'Qualys VMDR', 'Rapid7 InsightVM', 'AWS Inspector + Trivy').

questions.label: Malicious-code protection tooling
questions.help: AV / EDR platform (e.g., 'CrowdStrike Falcon', 'Microsoft Defender for Endpoint', 'SentinelOne', 'Carbon Black').

questions.label: System monitoring / detection tooling
questions.help: IDS / IPS / NDR / EDR feeding monitoring (often the same tool as malware protection plus a network-side counterpart).

questions.label: Security alert / advisory source summary
questions.help: Brief phrase summarizing where alerts come from. Detail goes in the dedicated sub-section.

questions.label: Integrity verification mechanism (one-liner)
questions.help: How software / firmware / file integrity is verified (e.g., 'Tripwire FIM + signed Git tags + SBOM verification at build').

family_questions.label: Flaw Remediation (SI-2)
family_questions.description: Vulnerability scanning, patch evaluation, and remediation SLAs.

questions.label: Patch SLAs by severity
questions.help: Map CVSS / vendor severity to patch SLA. Example: 'Critical (CVSS 9.0+ or KEV catalog): 15 days; High (7.0–8.9): 30 days; Medium (4.0–6.9): 90 days; Low: best-effort.' Federal systems often follow BOD 22-01 timelines for KEVs.

questions.label: CISA KEV catalog handling
questions.help: How CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog drives expedited remediation. BOD 22-01 timelines if applicable. Reference for federal agencies.

questions.label: Patch evaluation + deployment workflow
questions.help: From CVE published → tested → CCB approved → deployed → verified. Reference §4 of the CM plan for the change workflow.

questions.label: Vulnerability exception process
questions.help: When a patch can't be applied within SLA: deviation request, compensating control, time-bound POA&M item.

family_questions.label: Malicious Code Protection (SI-3)
family_questions.description: AV / EDR coverage, signature management, and response on detection.

questions.label: Signature update cadence
options: Multiple times per day per vendor schedule

questions.label: User reporting channel for suspected malware
questions.help: How users report suspected malware (e.g., 'phish report button in email client; ServiceNow Security Incident form').

family_questions.label: System Monitoring (SI-4)
family_questions.description: IDS / IPS / EDR / NDR / WAF and what they monitor for.

questions.label: Alert routing destination
questions.help: Where SI-4 alerts land (typically SIEM + IR ticketing — see §4 of AU and IR plans).

questions.label: Coverage attestation cadence
questions.help: How often the org attests that all in-scope assets have monitoring agents installed and reporting.

family_questions.label: Security Alerts and Advisories (SI-5)
family_questions.description: Sources of advisories and how they're triaged.

questions.label: Advisory ingestion mechanism
questions.help: How advisories flow into the workflow (email distribution → triage → ticket; automated TIP / SOAR ingestion).

questions.label: Advisory triage SLA
questions.help: Time from advisory publication to triage decision (apply / not applicable / monitor / accept risk).

questions.label: Internal dissemination
questions.help: Who internal to the org receives advisories that affect this system (System Owner, Engineering, ISSO, CCB chair).

family_questions.label: Integrity Verification (SI-6, SI-7)
family_questions.description: Software / firmware / file integrity, and security-function verification.

questions.label: File integrity monitoring (FIM) tool
questions.help: Tool monitoring the filesystem for unauthorized changes (e.g., 'Tripwire', 'OSSEC / Wazuh', 'AIDE', 'Defender for Endpoint integrity rules').

questions.label: FIM scope
questions.help: Which files / directories are under FIM (system binaries, config dirs, web content, application code, etc.).

questions.label: Software / firmware integrity verification
questions.help: Code signing for installed software, signed package repositories, secure boot for firmware. Reference SBOM if applicable.

questions.label: Security-function verification cadence (SI-6)
questions.help: How often security functions (e.g., crypto, access control) are verified to be operating correctly.

family_questions.label: Input Validation (SI-10)
family_questions.description: How input from users, services, and external sources is validated.

questions.label: Input validation strategy
questions.help: Whitelist vs blacklist, schema validation, parameterized queries, OWASP ASVS alignment level.

questions.label: Validation enforcement layers
options: Client-side (UX hint only — never security boundary)

questions.label: Review cadence for validation rules
questions.help: How often validation rules are reviewed against new attack patterns (e.g., 'After each major release', 'Quarterly with security').

family_questions.label: Error Handling (SI-11)
family_questions.description: What's exposed in error messages vs what's logged for debugging.

questions.label: User-facing error policy
questions.help: What users see on errors. Best practice: generic messages with a correlation ID; sensitive details in logs only.

questions.label: Logged error content
questions.help: What's captured in audit / application logs (stack trace, query, parameters). Reference AU plan privacy_redaction for what's masked.

questions.label: Error log review cadence
questions.help: How often error logs are reviewed for new failure patterns / security signals.

family_questions.label: Information Management & Retention (SI-12)
family_questions.description: Lifecycle of information stored, processed, or transmitted by the system.

questions.label: Retention schedule reference
questions.help: NARA records schedule, organizational records-retention policy, or contractual reference (e.g., 'NARA GRS 4.2 for security records; per data-sharing-agreement Sec 8 for partner data').

questions.label: Disposal method
questions.help: How records are destroyed at end of retention. Reference NIST SP 800-88 r1 sanitization requirements + MP-6.

questions.label: Information quality controls (SI-18)
questions.help: How accuracy / completeness / currency of stored information is maintained, especially for PII (per SI-18).

family_questions.label: Integrity Scope and Coverage
family_questions.description: What's in scope for monitoring, scanning, and integrity protection.

questions.label: Total endpoints in scope
questions.help: Approximate count of hosts / containers / VMs requiring monitoring + AV/EDR coverage.

questions.label: External-facing components count
questions.help: Public-facing surface (web servers, APIs, etc.) — typically more frequently scanned.

questions.label: Data volume protected (approximate)
questions.help: Order of magnitude (e.g., '5 TB application data; ~50M user records').

family_questions.label: Integrity Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate SI control effectiveness.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: % KEV-catalog vulns affecting system + SLA compliance
Endpoint coverage rate (% reporting in last 24h)
Open POA&M items linked to SI controls

family_questions.label: Monitoring Coverage Verification
family_questions.description: How the org continuously verifies SI tooling is actually deployed everywhere it should be.

questions.label: Coverage-gap detection mechanism
questions.help: How assets without required SI agents are detected (CMDB ↔ EDR roster reconciliation; nightly diff job).

questions.label: Coverage-gap remediation SLA
questions.help: Time from detection to gap closed (e.g., 'Within 24h for production'; '7 days otherwise').

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the SI control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.10').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for SI findings
questions.help: Convention for SI-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-SI-' for general; 'POAM-SI2-' for vuln-specific).

questions.label: AU event handoff
questions.help: How SI-4 monitoring events flow into the audit pipeline (SIEM index, log sources, retention).

questions.label: IR signal handoff
questions.help: How SI-3 / SI-4 / SI-7 detections become incidents in the IR plan workflow.

questions.label: RA-5 vulnerability data consumption
questions.help: How SI-2 flaw remediation consumes RA-5 vulnerability scans. Tooling, frequency, ticket queue.

questions.label: CM change-workflow integration
questions.help: How patches feed through the CM-3 change-control workflow. Emergency-patch pathway.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying SI continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

prompts: Reference §4.2 — vuln scan tool, cadence, and patch SLAs by severity.
Document CISA KEV-catalog handling and BOD 22-01 timelines if applicable.
Address coordination with CM change-control (CM-3) — see CM Plan §4.1.
Document emergency-patch pathway for active exploitation.
Reference SI-2(2) automated flaw remediation status, SI-2(3) time to remediate / benchmarks, SI-2(5) automatic software / firmware updates, SI-2(6) removal of previous versions.
evidence_suggestions: Vulnerability-scan results (last cycle, redacted as needed)

extra_fields.label: KEV compliance tracking method
extra_fields.help: How affected KEVs are identified for this system and tracked to BOD 22-01 deadline (or organizational equivalent).

extra_fields.label: Emergency-patch pathway
extra_fields.help: Expedited workflow for actively-exploited vulnerabilities. CCB retroactive review window.

prompts: Reference §4.3 — coverage, signature update cadence, detection modes, response action.
Address allowlisting / application control coordination if used (overlaps CM-7).
Document handling of false positives that block legitimate operations.
Reference SI-3(8) detect unauthorized commands, SI-3(10) malicious code analysis.
evidence_suggestions: EDR / AV deployment console showing coverage

extra_fields.label: Allowlist / application-control coordination
extra_fields.help: How SI-3 (malware protection) coordinates with CM-7 (least functionality) allowlisting (e.g., 'EDR enforces signature + behavior; WDAC enforces allowlist; both bypassed only via CCB approval').

extra_fields.label: Malicious-code analysis capability (SI-3(10))
options: External IR retainer for novel samples

prompts: Reference §4.4 — monitoring layers, events monitored, alert routing.
Address monitoring strategy (continuous vs sampling, breadth vs depth).
Document protection of the monitoring tools themselves (tamper-evidence, RBAC).

Reference SI-4(2) automated tools for real-time analysis, SI-4(4) inbound + outbound communications traffic, SI-4(5) system-generated alerts, SI-4(11) wireless intrusion detection, SI-4(14) wireless intrusion detection systems, SI-4(20) privileged users, SI-4(22) unauthorized network services.

extra_fields.label: Protection of monitoring tools themselves
extra_fields.help: Tamper protection on the monitoring infrastructure: who can disable agents, who can edit detection rules, audit-trail of changes.

extra_fields.label: Inbound + outbound traffic monitoring (SI-4(4))
extra_fields.help: How both ingress and egress traffic are monitored. Cloud-native (VPC flow logs, Azure NSG flow logs) and traditional (IDS taps, SPAN ports).

prompts: Reference §4.5 — sources, ingestion, triage SLA, dissemination.
Document the role responsible for monitoring advisory feeds.
Address coordination with the CISA KEV catalog (overlaps SI-2).
Reference SI-5(1) automated alerts and advisories ingestion.

extra_fields.label: Advisory-monitoring role
extra_fields.help: Role accountable for monitoring advisory feeds (e.g., 'Vulnerability Management Team Lead').

prompts: Reference §4.6 — FIM tool, scope, software / firmware integrity verification.
Document signed-package verification at install / update time.
Address SBOM generation and consumption.
Reference SI-7(1) integrity checks at startup + at defined frequency, SI-7(7) integration of detection and response, SI-7(15) code authentication.

extra_fields.label: SBOM approach
extra_fields.help: Whether and how SBOMs are generated (build-time tooling, format, where stored) and consumed (vulnerability matching, license-compliance checking). Reference EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18 for federal context.

extra_fields.label: Code authentication (SI-7(15))
extra_fields.help: Cryptographic verification of code authenticity prior to execution. Sigstore, Authenticode, vendor signing, internal CA.

prompts: Reference §4.7 — validation strategy, enforcement layers, ASVS alignment.
Document handling of structured (JSON / XML) and unstructured (free text) inputs separately.
Address the WAF rule maintenance cadence if WAF is in scope.
Reference SI-10(3) predictable behavior, SI-10(5) restrict inputs to trusted sources, SI-10(6) injection prevention.
evidence_suggestions: Sample integration test for validation rules

extra_fields.label: Injection prevention approach (SI-10(6))
extra_fields.help: Specific mitigations for SQL / OS / LDAP / NoSQL / template / XPath injection. Parameterized queries, ORM, escape contexts, etc.

prompts: Reference §4.8 — user-facing vs logged error content.
Address sensitive information that must NEVER appear in logs (passwords, full PII, session tokens) — coordinate with AU plan privacy_redaction.
Document correlation IDs that let users / support reference an error without revealing internals.
Reference SI-11 ODV — organization-defined personnel or roles to whom error information is revealed.
evidence_suggestions: Sample stack trace from production logs (showing redaction)

extra_fields.label: Correlation ID strategy
extra_fields.help: How a single user-action error gets tied to its server-side log entries (request ID propagation, distributed-trace ID).

extra_fields.label: Log review for error patterns
extra_fields.help: Cadence for reviewing error logs for new failure patterns or security signals.

prompts: Reference §4.9 — information categories, retention schedule, disposal method.
Address quality controls for PII (SI-18) if applicable.
Document data classification labels in use.
Reference SI-12(1) limit personally identifiable information elements, SI-12(2) minimize personally identifiable information in testing, training, and research, SI-12(3) information disposal.

extra_fields.label: PII minimization in test / training (SI-12(2))
extra_fields.help: How production PII is excluded / synthesized for non-production environments. Tooling and verification.

extra_fields.label: Disposal certification process (SI-12(3))
extra_fields.help: Chain of custody and certificate of destruction for disposed information / media. References MP-6.

glossary.definition: Detection of malicious activity by recognizing patterns of behavior (process injection, lateral movement, privilege escalation) rather than file signatures.
CISA Binding Operational Directive 22-01, requiring federal agencies to remediate vulnerabilities in the CISA KEV catalog within specified timeframes.
Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures — a unique identifier assigned to a publicly disclosed vulnerability.
Common Vulnerability Scoring System — a numerical score (0.0–10.0) reflecting the severity of a CVE based on exploitability and impact.
Dynamic Application Security Testing — runtime testing of a deployed application by sending crafted inputs and observing behavior.
Endpoint Detection and Response — security tooling deployed on hosts that collects telemetry, detects threats, and supports incident response.
An alert that, on investigation, was not a real security event. False-positive tuning is a continuous calibration.
File Integrity Monitoring — tooling that detects unauthorized changes to specified files / directories.
Detection that uses rules and characteristics (rather than exact signatures) to identify suspected malicious content. Higher recall but more false positives.
Intrusion Detection System / Intrusion Prevention System. IDS alerts on observed attacks; IPS additionally blocks them.
CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog — a curated list of CVEs known to be actively exploited. BOD 22-01 mandates expedited federal remediation.
Software designed to perform unauthorized actions or compromise the integrity, availability, or confidentiality of a system. Includes malware, viruses, worms, ransomware, trojans, rootkits, etc.
Managed Detection and Response — a service combining technology (typically EDR) with human analysts who triage alerts on the customer's behalf.
Mean Time to Patch — average duration from a patch becoming available to deployment in the system.
Application Security Verification Standard — OWASP framework for verifying web-application security at three assurance levels.
A software update that addresses a specific defect, often a security vulnerability.
Runtime Application Self-Protection — security instrumentation embedded in an application that detects and blocks attacks at runtime.
Malicious code that encrypts or exfiltrates data and demands payment for restoration or non-disclosure.
Static Application Security Testing — analysis of application source code (or compiled binary) to identify security defects without executing it.
Software Bill of Materials — a formal record of components and dependencies in a piece of software. Required for federal software per EO 14028 / OMB M-22-18.
Software Composition Analysis — examining the third-party components in an application for known vulnerabilities and license compliance.
A pattern (file hash, byte sequence, network packet pattern) that uniquely identifies a known threat. Used by signature-based detection engines.
Per SI-20, deliberately marking information so that unauthorized exfiltration or modification can be detected. Generally used in high-risk classified contexts.
Web Application Firewall — a filter applied to HTTP / HTTPS traffic that detects and blocks application-layer attacks like SQL injection and cross-site scripting.
A vulnerability that is exploited before the vendor / public is aware (i.e., zero days of advance notice). Particularly dangerous because no patch exists at exploitation time.
